source_text: ΤΟΥ ΕΝΑΓΙΟΙΣ ΠΑΤΡΟΣ ΗΜΩΝ ΑΘΑΝΑΣΙΟΥ. Τοῖς τὸν μονήρη βίον ἀσκοῦσι, καὶ ἐν πίστει Θεοῦ ἱδρυμένοις, ἀγαπητοῖς καὶ ποθεινοτάτοις ἀδελφοῖς ἐν Κυρίῳ χαίρειν. Εὐχαριστῶ μὲν τῷ Κυρίῳ, τῷ δόντι ὑμῖν εἰς αὐτὸν πιστεῦσαι, ἵνα μετὰ τῶν ἁγίων καὶ ὑμεῖς ἔχητε τὴν ζωὴν τὴν αἰώνιον· ἐπειδὴ δέ εἰσί τινες οἱ τὰ Ἀρείου φρονοῦντες, περιερχόμενοι τὰ μοναστήρια, δι' οὐδὲν ἄλλο εἰ μὴ ἵνα, ὡς πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐλθόντες καὶ ἀφ' ἡμῶν ὑποστρέφοντες, τοὺς ἀκεραίους ἐξαπατῶσι· τινὲς δέ εἰσιν οἱ διαβεβαιοῦντες μὲν τὰ Ἀρείου μὴ φρονεῖν, συγκαταβαίνοντες δὲ, καὶ μετ' αὐτῶν εὐχόμενοι ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό· ἀναγκαίως, παρακελευόντων τινῶν εἰλικρινεστάτων ἀδελφῶν, πρὸς ὑμᾶς γράφειν ἐσπούδασα, ἵνα τὴν εὐσεβῆ πίστιν, ἣν ἡ τοῦ Θεοῦ χάρις ἐν ὑμῖν ἐργάζεται, ἀκεραίως καὶ ἀδόλως φυλάττοντες, οὐ μὴ πρόφασιν δῶτε σκανδάλου τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς. Ὅταν γάρ τινες ὑμᾶς τοὺς ἐν Χριστῷ πιστοὺς θεωρήσαντες μετ' αὐτῶν συνερχομένους καὶ κοινωνοῦντας, πάντως ὑπονοήσαντες ἀδιάφορον εἶναι τὸ τοιοῦτον, εἰς τὸν τῆς ἀσεβείας ἐμπεσοῦνται βόρβορον. Ἵν' οὖν μὴ τοῦτο γένηται, θελήσατε, ἀγαπητοὶ, τοὺς μὲν φανερῶς φρονοῦντας τὰ τῆς ἀσεβείας ἀποστρέφεσθαι, τοὺς δὲ νομίζοντας τὰ Ἀρείου μὴ φρονεῖν, κοινωνοῦντας δὲ μετὰ τῶν ἀσεβῶν φυλάττεσθαι· καὶ μάλιστα ὧν τὸ φρόνημα ἀποστρεφόμεθα, τούτους ἀπὸ τῆς κοινωνίας προσήκει φεύγειν. Εἰ δέ τις προσποιεῖται μὲν ὁμολογεῖν ὀρθὴν πίστιν, φαίνεται δὲ κοινωνῶν ἐκείνοις, τὸν τοιοῦτον προτρέψασθε ἀπέχεσθαι τῆς τοιαύτης συνηθείας· καὶ ἐὰν μὲν ἐπαγγέλληται, ἔχετε τὸν τοιοῦτον ὡς ἀδελφόν· ἐὰν δὲ φιλονείκως ἐπιμένῃ, τὸν τοιοῦτον παραιτεῖσθε. Οὕτω γὰρ διατελοῦντες καθαρὰν τὴν πίστιν διατηρήσετε· κἀκεῖνοι βλέποντες ὑμᾶς ὠφεληθήσονται, φοβηθέντες μὴ ἄρα ὡς ἀσεβεῖς καὶ τὰ ἐκείνων φρονοῦντες νομισθῶσιν.
thought_title: Shun the impious and guard against those who commune with them
orientation: Athanasius opens his letter to the monks, greeting them and explaining why he writes: to warn them against Arians and those who pray with Arians.
pass_a_gloss: Of our father among the saints Athanasius. To those practicing the monastic life and established in faith in God, beloved and most longed-for brothers in the Lord, greetings. I thank the Lord, who gave you to believe in him, so that with the saints you too may have eternal life; but since there are some who hold the views of Arius, going around the monasteries, for no other reason except so that, coming to you and returning from us, they may deceive the simple; and there are some who insist that they do not hold the views of Arius, but joining them and praying with them together; necessarily, since some most sincere brothers urged me, I have hastened to write to you, so that guarding the true faith, which the grace of God works in you, purely and without guile, you may never give a pretext of stumbling block to the brothers. For whenever some see you, the faithful in Christ, coming together with them and sharing communion, certainly suspecting that such a thing is a matter of indifference, they will fall into the mire of impiety. So that this may not happen, be willing, beloved, to turn away from those who openly hold the things of impiety, and to guard against those who think they do not hold the views of Arius but share communion with the impious; and especially those whose mindset we turn away from, these it is fitting to flee from their communion. But if someone pretends to confess the true faith, yet is seen sharing communion with those, urge such a one to abstain from such habitual association; and if he promises, hold such a one as a brother; but if he stubbornly persists, reject such a one. For continuing in this way you will keep the faith pure; and those seeing you will be benefited, fearing lest they be reckoned as impious and as holding those views.

choices.why: Glossary requires 'monastic life' for this fixed term.
Glossary requires 'joining them' for this term, capturing the active condescension to the Arians' level.
Glossary requires 'together' for this phrase, indicating praying at the same place.
Glossary requires 'the simple' for those easily deceived.
Glossary requires 'true faith' for the orthodox faith.
Glossary requires 'habitual association' for the custom of associating with the impious.

pass_b_english: Our father among the saints Athanasius. To those practicing the monastic life, grounded in faith in God, beloved and most longed-for brothers in the Lord, greeting. I thank the Lord, who gave you faith in him, so that you too may have eternal life with the saints. But since there are some who hold the views of Arius and go around the monasteries for no other reason than to come to you and then return from us, deceiving the simple, and since there are others who insist they do not hold the views of Arius yet join them and pray together with them, I have necessarily been eager to write to you, urged on by some very sincere brothers. I write so that, keeping the true faith that God's grace works in you purely and without guile, you may never give the brothers any occasion for a stumbling block.

For whenever some see you, who are faithful in Christ, gathering with them and sharing communion, they will certainly suspect that such a thing makes no difference, and they will fall into the mire of impiety. So that this may not happen, beloved, resolve to shun those who openly hold the views of impiety, and keep yourselves from those who think they do not hold the views of Arius yet share communion with the impious. And especially those whose mindset we reject, it is fitting to flee from communion with them.

But if someone pretends to confess the true faith yet is seen sharing communion with them, urge that person to abstain from such habitual association. If he promises, treat him as a brother. But if he stubbornly persists, reject him. For by continuing in this way you will keep your faith pure, and those who see you will benefit, fearing lest they be reckoned as impious and as holding those views.

problems.source_quote: ΤΟΥ ΕΝΑΓΙΟΙΣ ΠΑΤΡΟΣ ΗΜΩΝ ΑΘΑΝΑΣΙΟΥ. Τοῖς τὸν μονήρη βίον ἀσκοῦσι, καὶ ἐν πίστει Θεοῦ ἱδρυμένοις, ἀγαπητοῖς καὶ ποθεινοτάτοις ἀδελφοῖς ἐν Κυρίῳ χαίρειν.
problems.why: Opening title and epistolary greeting completely omitted.
problems.fix: Our father among the saints Athanasius. To those practicing the monastic life, grounded in faith in God, beloved and most longed-for brothers in the Lord, greeting.

problems.why: ἀφ' ἡμῶν means 'from you/away from you,' not 'from us.'
φυλάττεσθαι here means 'keep yourselves from' or 'beware of,' not 'guard against' in the sense of watching for danger; it's about self-protection through avoidance.

problems.quote: Especially when we reject someone's mindset, it is fitting to flee from their communion
problems.source_quote: καὶ μάλιστα ὧν τὸ φρόνημα ἀποστρεφόμεθα, τούτους ἀπὸ τῆς κοινωνίας προσήκει φεύγειν
problems.why: Misconstrued syntax: ὧν is genitive plural, 'those whose'; ἀποστρεφόμεθα is 'we shun/turn away from'; τούτους is accusative object of φεύγειν. Meaning: 'and especially those whose mindset we reject, it is fitting to flee from communion with them.'
problems.fix: and especially those whose mindset we reject, it is fitting to flee from communion with them

problems.ruling: ἐπαγγέλληται means 'promises/undertakes,' not merely 'agrees'; the nuance of making a commitment is lost.
